Former Lagos State Governor, Babatunde Fashola, has challenged opposition parties to openly declare their intention to scrap the Nigerian Education Loan Fund if they take power, saying students and families benefiting from the scheme would resist such a move. Fashola said the student loan scheme was one of the interventions introduced by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration to ease the cost-of-living burden on Nigerian families. He stated this while defending the Federal Government’s response to economic hardship, arguing that the NELFUND scheme had helped families meet education expenses without having to pay the full cost from their disposable income. “I challenge the opponents to come and say they are going to cancel NELFUND and see how the people and the students who are benefiting from it and the families will vote. I know they won’t dare to,” he said. He said the initiative was designed to reduce the financial pressure on families by supporting students with school fees and providing upkeep allowances. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Your disposable income goes to rent, transport, healthcare and your children’s education. NELFUND was, ‘we will help families in need to pay school fees. Instead of dipping money out of their pockets to pay, we will give that support,’” Fashola said. He added that more than one million beneficiaries had benefited from the scheme, with the number continuing to increase. The former governor also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of the rising cost of living, describing inflationary pressures as a global challenge worsened by the COVID-19 pandemic, the Russia-Ukraine war and the conflict in the Middle East. According to him, supply disruptions following the pandemic and the wars had contributed to rising prices across countries, including Nigeria. “There’s no need denying the fact that the cost-of-living challenge is now a global challenge, and anybody who is right-thinking will concede that,” he said. Fashola said the Federal Government had responded to the situation through measures including the review of the minimum wage, the introduction of NELFUND and tax reforms. He, however, argued that increasing people’s income alone could not address the economic challenges, warning that excessive cash injections could fuel inflation. “Every economist worth his salt will tell you that you can’t throw cash at all of the problem all the time. Otherwise, you create hyper-demand inflation,” he said. Christabel Ndoeche
